system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
### Buyer review of Seller positions

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation & one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | Aggregate general Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | **25% / AUD 6m**. The 20% fallback requires prior written approval from Amelia Frost identifying the draft; none is given. | **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6m.** The proposed fallback is not authorised. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | **AUD 25,000** de minimis; **AUD 250,000** basket, with recovery only above the basket. | **AUD 5,000** de minimis; **AUD 50,000** aggregate basket, with liability from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject; counter to playbook thresholds.** The Seller’s thresholds are materially higher and its excess-only recovery is contrary to the Buyer’s position. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | **18 months** after Completion; proposes applying limitations to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | **24 months** after Completion for general claims; 18 months requires Amelia Frost’s written approval, which has not been given. | **Reject; counter at 24 months and confine the period to general claims.** The proposed period is an unauthorised fallback and must not override separate regimes. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits. | Separate Fundamental/Title regime: **100% cap, at least six years**, outside general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject; require the separate regime.** Applying general limits would materially weaken recovery for core ownership and authority risks. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Reject; expressly preserve the carve-out.** The Seller’s blanket wording would improperly restrict claims for serious misconduct. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records, plus specific disclosures. | Require **specific fair disclosure**; reject deemed disclosure of the whole data room, public registers or matters found by prudent search. | **Reject the general-disclosure approach; require specific fair disclosure.** Broad incorporation would make it unclear what was actually disclosed against each warranty. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | Delete blanket knowledge exclusions; if any qualifier remains, use named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry and never apply it to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Reject; delete the blanket exclusion.** It turns access or constructive discoverability into a broad bar on claims. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller will use reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. | Require **effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion**; reasonable endeavours alone are insufficient. | **Reject; make both consent and condition-satisfaction evidence Completion requirements.** The disclosure says neither final consent nor condition evidence is currently included, and Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** facility to be addressed by a release after Completion. | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; any post-Completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval. | **Reject post-Completion release as drafted; require payout, repayment and effective releases at Completion.** The disclosure confirms no repayment or final discharge is currently included. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD **420,000** bonuses are the Seller’s matter and are not separately itemised in the funds flow. | Include the **AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs** as a specific line item or have the Seller fund them; reconcile the funds flow. | **Require itemisation or Seller funding before agreeing funds flow.** The disclosed bonuses are conditional, absent from the draft funds flow and may carry unquantified on-costs. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and considered adequate. | Broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; treat **AUD 180,000** as unverified either way. | **Reject the narrow indemnity; broaden it without removing the SOW3 cure.** Transfer depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee, while the open amount is not independently verified and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material. | Preserve logs, investigate and provide updates; do not assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified demand. | **Do not accept a materiality conclusion; require preservation, investigation and updates.** The disclosure leaves access, scope and notification obligations unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling **AUD 330,000** are ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess the renewals; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **Seek detail and assess; do not automatically classify as Debt or deduct from price.** The disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations and exclusive-remedy/non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; Seller says Tax/IP positions are settled under the general regime. | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override. | **Reject blanket application; preserve separate category treatment and leave Tax/IP open.** The Seller’s umbrella wording could silently override distinct protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on the Company share register at DD-012 as evidence of 100% title. | Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority; DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof. | **Do not treat DD-012 as sufficient; request independent verification.** The register identifies the Seller as holder but does not establish independent verification. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers Tax and IP warranties settled under the general regime. | Keep Tax/IP terms open; assume neither unlimited liability nor resolution. | **Do not accept as settled; continue negotiation on separate terms.** The Seller’s assertion is not Buyer approval or authority to resolve these terms. |
=== END ADVICE ===
